answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity in time. Make every account's mining yield grow with its age, like cedar stands whose timber becomes harvestable only after seasons of growth: a fresh wallet lies near-worthless on the tundra of the ledger, and a million sown clones stay thin saplings because unlocks rise epoch by epoch. Sybils then face a nursery problem, since the cost of seeding and tending thousands of young accounts exceeds what any pays out until it has genuinely matured, so honest old-growth agents outearn every cloned grove.
